title: CRISPR for tauopathy
text:
Approximately 9% of fatal and incurable Alzheimer’s-related disease frontotemporal dementia (FTD) cases are
caused by mutations in MAPT. The goal of this work is to develop our novel CRISPR genome editing platform
to remove the mutant MAPT allele, leaving the non-diseased allele intact, in human cells and mice. We will
evaluate and optimize our editing strategy in patient iPSCs and induced neurons, determine whether pathology
can be reversed or only prevented in a mouse model of FTD and characterize loss of 3 embedded regulatory
regions in MAPT that may be disrupted by gene targeting therapies.

title: BRAIN CONNECTS: FAST-ET: fast automated serial tape-enabled electron tomography
text:
The goal of this proposal is to advance the scalability and automation of electron tomography (ET) to achieve
multi-resolution, large-scale imaging of the brain. By integrating automated tape-based sample handling,
advanced ET technologies, and machine learning techniques for data acceleration and augmentation, we aim to
comprehensively map neuronal circuits, and deliver a paradigm shift for generating mammalian whole-brain
connectomes. Mapping the detailed organization and connectivity of the brain will provide critical insights into
principles of neuronal circuit organization and a foundation for understanding how they are altered in
neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Advancing Renal Mass Diagnosis and Management through AI-Enhanced Decision Support Systems (RMM-DSS)
text:
Renal masses are increasingly detected incidentally, and current clinical approaches often result in unnecessary
surgeries for benign lesions—particularly those under 4 cm—posing avoidable risks to patients. This project will
develop and evaluate AI-enhanced tools that integrate multimodal real-world data (RWD) to improve the
diagnosis, risk stratification, and management of renal masses. By supporting more accurate and personalized
decision-making, the proposed system has the potential to reduce overtreatment, improve patient outcomes,
and inform future clinical guidelines.

title: Long-Term Trajectories of Accelerated Biological Aging and Functional Decline Associated with Breast Cancer and its Treatment
text:
By understanding how cancer treatments alter the course of biological and functional aging in cancer survivors,
our study can help to guide patient care. Specifically, our study will help identify patients at risk for long-term
physical function impairment as a result of cancer treatment, provide clues as to the biological mechanisms
through which these adverse effects occur, and inform future strategies to mitigate these effects.

title: In Vivo 3-D Multi-Isotope Autoradiography of Radiopharmaceutical Therapy
text:
A novel imaging system will be developed to facilitate the investigation and understanding of a
cutting-edge cancer treatment method known as radiopharmaceutical therapy. This new imaging system will
offer capabilities that are currently unavailable through existing methods. Its introduction is expected to
significantly enhance the development of radiopharmaceutical therapy for various types of cancers.

title: Genome-wide chromatin structure and function in Kaposi Sarcoma tissue
text:
The Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus infects cells and causes changes that promote the
development and maintenance of cancer; enhancers are pieces of the human genome that turn on and off genes
to control cell growth. Mapping enhancers in actual tumor tissue from patients will identify DNA sequences
and proteins that may be effective targets in cancer therapy. This project combines a resourced specimen
repository, an equipped technological core facility, and undergraduate student research to understand how this
virus activates the human genome in patient tumors.

title: Role of bacterial-derived small molecules in immunotherapy
text:
Lung and bronchial cancer cause more deaths in the U.S. than any other type of cancer in both men and
women. The project will characterize and develop bacterial-derived metabolites that synergize with the anti-
PD1 immune checkpoint inhibitor. This knowledge will serve to develop novel agents acting as potential
adjuvants for the treatment and management of NSCLC.

title: Rapid Tests for Recent Infection (RTRI) for Precision Public Health in Sub-Saharan Africa: Next-Generation Strategies Amid Changing HIV Epidemiology
text:
HIV is a top cause of death in sub-Saharan Africa, but rates of new infections are declining, so that HIV
prevention services avert fewer infections per client served, and HIV testing services lead to fewer new HIV-
positive diagnoses per test conducted. To increase the efficiency of these services, a rapid point-of-care test
for recent HIV infection has been developed and is being used in over two-thirds of people newly diagnosed
with HIV in Zambia in order to identify other people at risk or living with undiagnosed HIV in their social
networks. We will use mathematical modeling to determine whether recency testing can help Zambia achieve
epidemic goals, is a good use of limited resources, and can be improved upon using “big data” methods for
greater precision, ease-of-use, and avoidance of potentially stigmatizing data elements.

title: Integrated Treatment of Adolescents with Substance Use Disorders and PTSD
text:
Substance use disorders (SUD) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) are debilitating and chronic
psychiatric disorders that frequently co-occur and often begin during adolescence or childhood. Early
intervention is crucial to prevent long-lasting negative health outcomes associated with co-occurring
SUD/PTSD in adulthood, but empirical research on integrated treatments for adolescents with co-occurring
SUD/PTSD is limited. The proposed study directly addresses this critical gap by evaluating an integrated,
trauma-focused intervention, Concurrent Treatment of PTSD and Substance Use Disorders using Prolonged
Exposure (COPE), specifically adapted for adolescents (COPE-A) with co-occurring SUD/PTSD.

title: MARVELOUS: Maternal RSV Vaccination- Evaluating Optimal Immune Responses
text:
This project leverages the recently-approved maternal Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) vaccine and large
datasets reflecting pregnancy vaccination against other respiratory pathogens to define key rules of immune
protection across the maternal-fetal dyad. We will characterize the protection that occurs both through direct
alterations to the fetal immune system, and through placental and breastmilk transfer of maternal antibodies.
These experiments will provide critical data to ensure optimal protection of mothers and infants from existing and
emerging pathogens.

title: Understanding the role of the gut-brain axis in modulating Cadmium neurotoxicity
text:
Cadmium (Cd) is a potential neurotoxicant positively associated with cognitive impairments and
neurodegenerative diseases in humans. Since the gut microbiome is a target of Cd toxicity and
the gut-brain axis is important for regulating neurological functions, this project aims to
determine the role of the gut-brain axis in regulating Cd neurotoxicity. This project will determine
for the first time the importance of the gut-brain axis in Cd-induced neurotoxicity, enhance the
understanding concerning the neurotoxicity of Cd and other environmental toxicants, and
provide translational implications for the design of prevention and intervention strategies to
mitigate Cd neurotoxicity by reprogramming the gut microbiome.

title: Decellularized cartilage and progenitor cells for laryngotracheal reconstruction
text:
Close to 10% of the over 20,000 premature children every year develop airway disorders that often require
laryngotracheal reconstruction using cartilage harvested from the rib cage, but this approach is invasive and
cannot be applied to younger children, which motivates an urgent need for new, improved technology. We
propose an innovative approach to produce functional cartilage for grafting using decellularized meniscus from
a cadaveric donor where selective digestion of tissue components creates channels for recellularization with
autologous cell sources obtained by a minimally invasive biopsy. The in vitro and in vivo proposed studies are
aimed at defining new, less invasive and more effective therapeutic options for laryngotracheal reconstruction.

title: Racially-associated MRI analysis and modeling for predicting aggressive prostate cancer
text:
In African Americans, prostate cancer is characterized by higher aggressiveness, more extensive metastases, early-
onset, and increased mortality rates than those in Caucasian Americans. We hypothesize that the racial disparity in
prostate cancer diagnosis can be reduced by using racially associated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) analysis.
The proposed MRI-based analysis model will be evaluated for men of different racial/ethnic characteristics at the
University of California Los Angeles (UCLA) and the University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB).

title: Relationships between APP and Mitochondria
text:
Mitochondrial dysfunction and failure of mitochondrial degradation pathways (mitophagy) are observed
in Alzheimer’s diseases (AD) and likely contribute to pathogenesis. Amyloid precursor protein (APP) localizes
to mitochondria and affects mitochondrial and mitophagy function. We will directly test the relationship between
APP, mitophagy, and mitochondrial function.

title: Intracellular and Extracellular Tau as Drivers of Lysosomal Failure in Human Neuronal Models of Frontotemporal Dementia
text:
This research and training plan will define the cascade of events that trigger lysosomal failure preceding Tau
aggregation, an early driver of neurodegeneration. During the K99 phase, I will train in cryo-electron
microscopy, proteomics, and lysosomal assays to map Tau–lysosome interactions at high resolution to define
the molecular mechanisms by which intracellular phosphorylated Tau disrupts lysosomal clearance in human
iPSC-derived neurons. In my R00 phase, I will test whether Tau aggregates impact lysosomal vulnerability and
whether pharmacological interventions can restore key phenotypes, laying the groundwork for future therapies.

title: Optimizing Clinical Documentation Quality in Hospital Obstetric Care
text: Variations in perinatal care quality and outcomes persist in the United States, yet no studies have identified how clinical documentation patterns may influence pregnancy care for women and newborns. The proposed study will use natural language processing, a data science approach, to identify documentation patterns and to examine whether these patterns are associated with perinatal morbidity outcomes for pregnant women and newborns. This work will inform the development of clinical decision support, the education and training of clinicians, and the realignment of institutional policies to positively influence documentation quality and optimize patient care.

title: Next generation of delivery platform for Prime editors based on an RNA vector for Sickle cell disease: the “all-in-one” vector
text:
The proposed research will have a high impact in the field of medicine, as it will develop new prototype vectors
able to deliver the Prime Editor system efficiently, leading to the production of safer modified cells. In addition,
this research is relevant to public health, and it will have a meaningful impact on developing new regenerative
medicine and gene therapy approaches to treat monogenic diseases and other genetic diseases.

title: Core B. Biostatistics, Bioinformatics and Genetic Analysis (BBGA)
text: CORE B. BIOSTATISTICS, BIOINFORMATICS AND GENETIC ANALYSIS (BBGA) The Ohio State University Vision Sciences Research Core Program (OSU-VSRCP) has established scientific connections among the vision researchers across five academic units (i.e., College of Medicine (COM), College of Optometry (COO), College of Engineering, College of Veterinary Medicine, College of Arts and Sciences) and newly engaged Nationwide Children’s Hospital. Program Director (PD) Dr. Moroi has support and commitment from Deans and Chairs for equipment, data science, space, new and existing programs to enhance collaborations among NEI-funded PIs, facilitate gathering pilot data for future PIs, and subsidizes cost for access to the High-Performance Computing Cluster (HPCC) that is maintained by the Ohio Supercomputer Center (OSC), which is relevant for Core B. The synergy among the vision research community has been established with a monthly meeting group called ViSOR (Vision Sciences OSU Research). Synergy between the Cores has been defined with a Steering Committee, which is composed of the PD, Core Directors and Co- directors. This synergy between Cores will coincide with the monthly ViSOR meetings, and ad hoc as needed for operational issues and future equipment purchases. In addition, an Advisory Group has been established to give guidance to the Steering Committee. Core B, BBGA Core has two aims: Aim 1. Provide analytical assistance for analyses of vision research data. The BBGA Core will provide analytical expertise for research data arising from clinic-based and genetic studies, such as whole-exome sequence, whole-genome sequencing, bulk RNA-Seq, and scRNA-Seq projects. The biostatistics staff will work with investigators of clinical research projects to design well-powered studies; assist in data management; and provide rigorous statistical analysis, including the appropriate methodology to deal with the intricacies of the correlation of two eyes. Aim 2. Provide consultation, training, and access to specialized software for genetic analyses of vision research data. The BBGA Core Director and staff will provide tailored consultations to users for planning and conducting their genetics research and analyses. Best practices will be promoted for study design, sample size estimation, and power calculation for bioinformatic and genetic components of grant applications. Training in the use of and access to specialized software for genetics and genomics analyses will be available. The added values are access to skilled experts in vision science genetics, the latest computation facilities, and specialized software for genetic analysis. This proposed P30 Core B, BBGA intends to maximize efficiency, offer centralized access to equipment and expertise that would be difficult, costly or impractical to duplicate in individual labs, and use protocols to ensure best practices to perform science at the highest standard. The expected outcome is increased collaboration for successful new proposals with the shared overarching goal to prevent blindness, restore vision and develop cures for eye diseases.

title: GPR39 as a Therapeutic Target in Aging-Related Vascular Cognitive Impairment and Dementia
text:
The proposed studies will develop a small molecule drug that stimulates a receptor called GPR39
as a therapeutic for aging-related dementia due to diseases of small blood vessels in the brain.
This is the second most common type of dementia after Alzheimer's disease. The small molecule
works by improving blood flow in small blood vessels in the brain.
